title: Chapter 4 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of Blueprint visual scripting, from events and variables to communication and debugging.

questions.question: What do white wires represent in a Blueprint graph?
questions.explanation: White wires control the order in which nodes are executed. Coloured wires carry data values.

questions.question: Which Blueprint type is reusable across multiple levels?
questions.explanation: Blueprint Classes are assets that can be instanced in any level. Level Blueprints are tied to a single map.

questions.question: The Construction Script runs only when the game starts.
questions.explanation: The Construction Script runs in the editor whenever the Blueprint is placed or modified. The Event Graph handles runtime logic.

questions.question: Which node outputs a text message to the screen?
questions.explanation: Print String displays a message both on screen and in the output log, perfect for debugging.

questions.question: When does Event BeginPlay fire?
options: Once when the actor is spawned or level starts
questions.explanation: BeginPlay fires once after the actor is fully initialized, before the first Tick.

questions.question: What is the Delta Seconds output from Event Tick used for?
questions.explanation: Delta Seconds is the time since last frame, essential for smooth, frame‑rate independent movement.

questions.question: How do you call a custom event you created?
options: Drag the event node into the graph again
Use the 'Call Function' node and type the event name
Connect it directly to a Print String
questions.explanation: You call a custom event by placing a node with its name (or dragging from My Blueprint). It's essentially a function with no return value.

questions.question: To store a whole number like a score, you would use a(n) _____ variable.
questions.explanation: Integers hold whole numbers (no decimals). Float is for decimals.

questions.question: What does the 'Instance Editable' checkbox do for a variable?
options: Allows the variable to be set per instance in the level editor
Deletes the variable when the game starts
Hides the variable from the graph
questions.explanation: Instance Editable exposes the variable in the Details Panel for each placed instance, allowing unique values per actor.

questions.question: Which node splits execution based on a Boolean condition?
questions.explanation: Branch has True and False outputs, driven by a Boolean condition input.

questions.question: What does a Sequence node do?
options: Loops a set number of times
Executes multiple outputs in order from a single input
questions.explanation: Sequence fires several execution lines one after another, top to bottom.

questions.question: Which loop is specifically designed to iterate over an array?
questions.explanation: For Each Loop automatically processes each element of an array, providing the element and index.

questions.question: Delay node pauses the entire game, including other Blueprints.
questions.explanation: Delay is non‑blocking; only the specific execution chain is paused. Other Blueprints and the game world continue.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using a Function over duplicating nodes?
options: Functions can have multiple execution outputs
questions.explanation: Functions encapsulate logic into a single reusable node, making graphs cleaner and easier to update.

questions.question: How many execution outputs can a standard Function have?
questions.explanation: Functions have a single output execution pin. For multiple outputs, use a Macro.

questions.question: What does casting an actor reference do?
options: Creates a copy of the actor
Checks if the actor is of a specific class and provides access to its properties
Moves the actor to a new location
questions.explanation: Casting verifies the actor's type and returns a typed reference if successful, allowing access to class‑specific members.

questions.question: Which communication method is best for decoupling sender and receiver?
questions.explanation: Event Dispatchers allow broadcasting without knowing who listens, keeping Blueprints independent.

questions.question: What is a Blueprint Interface?
options: A graphical skin for the editor
A contract defining functions that Blueprints can implement
questions.explanation: Interfaces define function signatures that any Blueprint can implement, enabling communication without casting to specific classes.

questions.question: Which debugging tool pauses execution on a specific node?
questions.explanation: A breakpoint halts execution when reached, allowing you to inspect variables and step through code.

questions.question: What key do you press to step to the next node while debugging?
questions.explanation: F10 steps to the next node; F11 steps into functions.

questions.question: You can watch a variable's value during gameplay by right‑clicking it and selecting 'Watch This Value'.
questions.explanation: Watching a variable adds it to the Watch window for real‑time inspection when paused.

questions.question: What is a good practice for keeping Blueprint graphs readable?
options: Use as many nodes as possible
Use comment boxes and align nodes
Place all logic in the Event Graph
questions.explanation: Comment boxes, alignment, and straight wires improve readability. Functions and macros reduce clutter.

questions.question: To quickly add a reroute point on a wire, _____-click the wire.
questions.explanation: Double‑clicking a wire creates a reroute node, allowing you to route wires neatly.

questions.question: Which node alternates between two outputs each time it's called?
questions.explanation: Flip Flop toggles between A and B outputs on successive calls, perfect for toggling states.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Gate node?
options: To control whether execution can pass through
questions.explanation: A Gate can be Open or Closed, blocking or allowing execution flow based on logic.

questions.question: You can call functions from a Blueprint Interface on any actor that implements that interface without casting.
questions.explanation: Interfaces allow you to call functions directly on a reference, as long as the actor implements the interface.

questions.question: What happens if you forget to add a Delay node's Completed pin?
questions.explanation: Without connecting the Completed output, execution bypasses the delay and continues instantly.

questions.question: Which panel contains the list of variables and functions in a Blueprint?
questions.explanation: My Blueprint shows variables, functions, macros, and event dispatchers for the current Blueprint.

questions.question: How can you reduce performance cost when using casting?
options: Store the cast result in a variable after first cast
questions.explanation: Caching the typed reference avoids repeated casting, which is more efficient.

questions.question: To disable Event Tick in a Blueprint, change the 'Start with Tick Enabled' property in the _____ Defaults.
questions.explanation: In the Class Defaults (toolbar button), you can set 'Start with Tick Enabled' to false to save performance.
